content.thinking:
I'll plan the design as a large perched phoenix with wings spread in a V, roughly 1.2m body length and 3m wingspan, standing with talons grounded at y=0, keeping the implementation straightforward and robust.

For the skeleton, I'm setting up hips as root with a curved spine chain to the chest, plus neck, head, and tail chains. For the wings, I'm building shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip chains per side with feathers extruded along each bone, working out that the feather outlines need their plane oriented horizontally rather than vertically -- so the direction vector should be the feather's length axis, a horizontal perpendicular vector for width, and vertical for thickness, rather than the default orientation which would make feathers stand up as vertical plates.

I'm also figuring out the coloring approach: painting each feather with a gradient from gold to orange to red along its length, using a lit shading model since feathers mostly face upward, and dealing with the fact that paint functions need to know each feather's length to normalize the gradient properly -- considering caching paint factories by rounded length classes rather than creating a unique paint per feather.

Now I'm sketching out wing anatomy: roughly 9 primaries, 8 secondaries, plus two rows of covert feathers per wing, totaling around 100 feather extrusions which should stay well under triangle budget. I'm placing the key wing joints -- shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip -- for a raised wing pose spanning about 3.4 meters, and starting to work out the direction vectors for how primary feathers fan out from the wrist.

Still defining feather geometry...

Confirming bone accepts a Joint, I'm now sketching the wing chain with shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip points parented to the chest joint, checking that side detection and joint names line up correctly before moving to the spine chain from the hips.

Still defining the skeleton chain...

For the chest coloring I'll wrap a countershade gradient between the crimson back and gold belly inside the cel-shading function so it responds to lighting properly. Then for the head I'm adding a scaled sphere with a beak made of two cones for upper and lower jaw, plus a jaw joint positioned slightly forward and down from the head anchor.

Still placing head features...

Working out crest feather orientation...

Since extrusion may not auto-orthogonalize the axes, I decide to manually compute a perpendicular "up" vector for each feather's plane, then move on to defining a tapered, flame-like outline shape for the feathers using a series of width points along their length.

Still writing the feather geometry...

Designing the drooping tail with jointed segments tapering in radius, then adding a fan of seven long streamer feathers from the tail base, angled outward with slight droop so their ends stay above the floor.

Now I'm layering in two extra-long central streamers plus multiple feather layers varying in length and offset, then moving to the legs: hip joints bending forward through a knee to an ankle target near the ground, sized so the chain reaches without stretching straight.

For the feet, I'm adding golden-orange scale texturing and designing three forward toes plus one back toe as short rods with rounded tips touching the floor, each capped with a darker claw spike, making sure the lowest points sit right at ground level.

Overall the model stands about 1.95 units tall and 3.5 wide, with wing tips reaching ~1.7 and the crest peaking near 1.9 — oversized but fitting the fantasy phoenix feel. I'm planning the wing arm as a tapering sweep chain in red, relying on layered feather/covert rows rather than a membrane plate to fill out the wing surface, then moving to lay out the feather base rows along that sweep.

Working out feather placement along the arm by parameterizing t from shoulder to tip: secondaries occupy t 0.1–0.5 and primaries 0.5–1.0, with a piecewise angle function sweeping feathers from roughly 85° back near the shoulder down to about 18° near the tip to mimic a realistic raised, fanned wing shape, plus a slight upward rise component so the feathers tilt up as the arm lifts toward y 1.7.

Now I'm sizing each feather with a sinusoidal length curve peaking near t=0.6 and tapering at both ends, setting feather width, and laying out counts: 9 primaries, 9 secondaries, plus two covert rows of 14 each offset slightly forward and upward per row, totaling around 44 feathers per wing (88 total) plus tail and crest feathers for roughly 115 parts. I'm also considering adding flame-shaped SVG texture cards scattered across the body and chest as a fiery fringe detail.

For the flame cards, I'm scattering around 120 of them across the body with minimum spacing, varying lean and size, flowing backward, and applying a glow effect in the phoenix's own colors using a flame SVG with gradient fills. I'm also thinking about adding a glowing torus ring behind the phoenix as a pyro emblem, plus a handful of glowing ember shapes (octahedrons) floating nearby, and possibly a thin glowing disc on the ground beneath the feet for extra ambiance.

Working through the ring placement, I'm positioning it behind the body and adjusting its size and position so it reads clearly without being too disrupted by the tail feathers passing through it, settling on a reasonable radius and height even though some overlap with the tail is unavoidable. Now I'm adding gold filigree details -- a collar ring around the neck built by sweeping a tube along a closed catmull curve through frames sampled along the neck, plus plans for bracelets, a circlet with a gem on the head, and gold tassels to complete the ornamental look.

For the chest gem, I'm figuring out placement by raycasting against the body surface to find the correct front-facing point instead of hardcoding coordinates, then attaching an octahedron gem with a glowing stick setting. I decide to skip some more elaborate decorative elements like a head circlet and forehead decal to keep things simpler, and now I'm starting to write the actual import statements and type setup for the script.

Writing imports and palette constants...

Working out the cross products confirms the thickness direction stays perpendicular and upward, and since the outline is symmetric, the sign doesn't actually matter. I'm now defining the feather extrusion function and outline point types, then setting up tail feathers with directions based on the tail joint, and crest plumes that sweep back and upward from the head using elevation angles and sideways thickness vectors.

I'm spreading the five crest plumes laterally with small x offsets and giving them a wider flame-like outline with a bright tip color, then sketching an SVG gradient flame shape for the body texture with a red-orange-yellow gradient and a lighter inner highlight, making sure the tip sits at the top and the wide base at the bottom. Now I'm setting up scattered flame cards across the body surface using a seeded random generator with a minimum distance constraint.

Now I'm defining the lean, flow, bend, size, and spin parameters for these scattered cards, planning similar card scattering for the neck, and considering a glow effect on the card meshes for a bright emissive look. I'm also working out the gold wing-arm design with armlet rings at the wrist using a closed catmull sweep, and laying out the shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip joint chain coordinates for the wing structure with named joints and a swept tube shape parented to the chest.

Now I'm figuring out how to access the wing's joint position for attaching feather bones, checking wingspan proportions against the body height and scaling feather length down to about 0.85x so the overall span stays reasonable near 4 meters. I'm placing feathers along the wing chain up to the tip point, then moving on to define the tail joint chain with a curved catmull path tapering from the hips down to a tip point, sized with a tapering radius sweep.

I'm laying out the tail fan with multiple feather layers: a wide lower layer of nine feathers at varying yaw angles and lengths with a slight downward pitch, a shorter lifted upper layer, and a few long narrow central streamer feathers with minimal pitch drop, using different widths for wing versus tail feathers. For the legs, I'm setting the hip joint position and figuring out the limb function's bend parameter format, planning to pass a single bend direction for the two-segment leg chain.

I'm computing the leg chain geometry—confirming the hip-to-ankle distance fits within the segment lengths and setting a slight forward knee bulge—then defining names for the hip, knee, and ankle joints along with sweep radii and a gold scale-patterned cel paint. For the feet, I'm placing toe tip targets spreading outward with a longer middle toe and a shorter hind toe, using rounded rod geometry with gold coloring, then adding small dark claw spikes angled downward and backward from each toe tip, checking that the claw and rod radii keep things visually grounded at the toe bottoms.

Now I'm working on the gold anklet rings positioned along the leg chain, then moving to the head: placing the skull as a scaled sphere near the top of the neck with a countershaded orange-to-gold cel paint, followed by an upper beak spike extending forward and slightly downward in a rounded cone shape, and starting to define the lower jaw joint position relative to the head.

I'm computing the jaw spike aimed from the jaw joint to its tip, then figuring out eye placement using surface decals wrapped around the skull with mirrored azimuth positions for left and right, checking for valid hit results before applying them. Now I'm working out the base position for head crest plumes, offset upward and back from the head joint.

I'm skipping the forehead gem and circlet idea for now, moving on to plan a gold collar ring built from a chain of points swept around the neck at a given parametric position, with the ring radius matching the neck's taper. I'm also sketching out the torso sweep using a radius array along the spine chain, keeping the body color as a paint texture and considering a slight belly shift before moving on to body hit detection.

Now I'm setting up a ray hit on the chest to place a glowing octahedron gem embedded in a small gold cylinder base, computing the sink depth for each. Then I'm adding a halo made of a large torus ring plus a thinner inner ring, with eight small glowing octahedron runes spaced evenly around the outer ring at 45-degree intervals.

I'm checking that the halo sits far enough behind the body and wings to avoid clipping, settling on a position roughly a meter back. Then I'm scattering fourteen small glowing ember octahedrons randomly around the body, capping their height below the model's peak and attaching them to the hips bone, while estimating the final part and triangle counts stay reasonable.

Figuring out texel density for the painted feather cards and scattering more neck cards at a smaller scale, then starting to write the actual file structure with vector helpers and type filters. Writing wing chain code...

Still writing feather placement logic...

Setting up the hips joint as the root with its position and aim direction, treating it as the start of the spine chain without a role since it's the root itself.

The spine chain starts at the hips position, and the neck chain connects to the chest joint positioned above it. Now I'm defining the ember-colored materials before writing everything out.
